matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation and verify that they are equal. Without this check you may produce a syntactically correct but arithmetically false equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick move, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Leaving the equation unchanged after moving a stick, resulting in 19 = 14, which is still false.

matchstick.title: Preserve valid numeral shapes
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from or added to a Roman numeral, the resulting glyph must correspond to a valid Roman numeral. An invalid shape makes the whole equation invalid regardless of the arithmetic.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you modify a numeral, ensure the new shape matches a known numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from an X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you cannot replace a vertical stick with a diagonal or rotate a stick when moving it. The orientation must stay the same in the destination character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any stick relocation, keep the original orientation of the stick.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn a vertical I into a diagonal V by moving a diagonal stick onto it.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect only the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick). Changing more than two symbols violates the one‑stick rule.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning a move, count how many characters will change; it must be exactly two.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from one numeral to another and also altering the operator, affecting three characters.

matchstick.title: Maintain a valid equality
matchstick.principle: The final equation must contain exactly one ‘=’ sign, composed of two horizontal sticks. You may not modify, remove, or add sticks to the equality sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any transformation, never change the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal stick from ‘=’, turning it into a single ‘‑’ sign.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick between numerals, consider known one‑stick transformations (e.g., I↔II, V↔X) that keep both source and destination as valid numerals. Both characters must remain valid after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to adjust numeral values, look for these standard one‑stick changes.
matchstick.example: Changing VII to XII by moving a diagonal from V to make X, but forgetting that the source V becomes invalid.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: Provide the corrected equation as a single line prefixed with ‘Correct version of the equation:’, using uppercase letters and collapsing whitespace. The verifier extracts the last such line for comparison.
matchstick.example: Omitting the required prefix or adding extra spaces, causing the answer to be rejected.

matchstick.title: Plus-to-minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If the equation contains a ‘+’ operator, you can move its vertical stick to a numeral (or to another operator) to turn ‘+’ into ‘‑’ (or vice versa), adjusting the arithmetic accordingly. The destination must remain a valid numeral or operator after the addition.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present and a vertical stick can be relocated to fix the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from ‘+’ to a numeral but leaving the ‘+’ without its vertical, turning it into ‘‑’ while the destination numeral becomes invalid.

matchstick.title: Advanced numeral transformations: diagonal swaps and numeral deletion
matchstick.principle: When moving diagonal sticks, consider swapping them between X and V (or similar) so that both characters remain valid; you may also delete a diagonal from a numeral if the remainder is still a recognized numeral. Both source and destination must be valid after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a diagonal stick is involved in the move.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from X to V to make X into V, but leaving the source X as a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator transformation and relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from or to an operator, ensure the resulting operator(s) remain valid; you may convert ‘+’ to ‘‑’ by moving a vertical stick, or relocate an entire single‑stick operator (e.g., ‘‑’) to a different position, provided the original location no longer requires that operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation contains a single‑stick operator (like ‘‑’) or a multi‑stick operator (like ‘+’) and you need to change the arithmetic relationship.
matchstick.example: Removing the horizontal stick from a ‘‑’ sign and placing it on a numeral, which eliminates the minus operator and leaves the expression without the required operator.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on visual changes and forgets to recompute the numeric values after the move.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recompute both sides of the equation after any stick relocation and confirm equality before finalizing.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves sticks without checking whether the resulting glyph matches a known Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Apply the ‘Preserve valid numeral shapes’ principle to verify that both source and destination remain valid numerals.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes or adds sticks to operators without ensuring the operator stays recognizable.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Use the ‘Operator transformation and relocation’ principle to keep operators valid after any stick move.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes moves a stick but forgets to place it, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember the ‘Limit changes to two characters’ rule: every moved stick must have a clear source and destination.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Changing an operator’s stick count can produce a non‑operator glyph.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Apply the ‘Operator transformation and relocation’ principle to ensure any operator alteration yields a valid operator.
